rawContent: @A_NeedhamNYU Yes. This is a problem in every developed and developing country. The desperate desire for techno-optimism solutions, so that we don't have to fundamentally change our standard of living, is the only thing holding up action on #climatechange

A much needed & thoughtful review of IPCC report Global Warming of 1.5C by Troy Vettese. Picks apart both blind faith in BECSS (bioenergy with carbon capture & storage) & green growth, but still hails it as a revolutionary document. https://t.co/Dva8FPhzio #ClimateChange #envhist

New report finds that under Canada's federal climate framework, oil & gas companies will have an average of 80% of its emissions exempt from federal carbon pricing.
Canada's #climatechange promises are impossible as long as #tarsands production continues. https://t.co/llqO3aKMFP

If you're the type of person who usually passes over #climatechange stuff, you can't afford to ignore it anymore. You need to get informed and involved in the conversation in 2019. You will regret it if you don't. And so will your kids and your grandkids.

It's "the choices being made by global society, not physics, which is the obstacle to meeting [1.5C warming]".
Close... it's the choices made by societies in industrialized countries that is the obstacle. https://t.co/bVuiG6bHl0 #climatechange

The bankruptcy of the California utility company PG&E demonstrates that the next financial crisis could be caused by #climatechange.
Bring on the #NewGreenDeal!

For more than three decades, "the fossil fuel industry and the [U.S.] Farm Bureau worked to sow uncertainty about the scientific consensus on human-caused #climatechange and the economic consensus on how to solve the problem."

Thrilled to learn that #Muskoka has been awarded over $100,000 by Federation of Canadian Municipalities to help increase its capacity to adapt to the effects of #climatechange or reduce greenhouse emissions. Congrats @muskokawatershd!! https://t.co/66uyyjtEkc

In my contribution to the cross-posted @ActiveHist @ClimateHist @NiCHE_Canada nuclear series, I argue that only dramatic reductions in energy use, not new technology, will save humanity from #climatechange catastrophe.
https://t.co/E95OKiB9Py #envhist #energyhist

The reason people find it difficult to think about #climatechange and the future is that our understanding of human history is dominated by the idea of progress. https://t.co/wRBxdh9mfB #envhist #envhum
Global economic growth is outstripping our green efforts to tackle #climatechange. We need to consume a lot less stuff, so that we use a lot less energy. https://t.co/2yVXQSbBe6

Yhe impacts of #climatechange extend beyond the irreversible damage to natural ecosystems. They will affect every aspect of human life. Nice review of The Uninhabitable Earth. https://t.co/wESaIt0Npt #envhist

New research suggests that sharp & potentially devastating temp rises of 3-5C in Arctic are now inevitable even if world succeeds in drastically cutting greenhouse gas emissions.
We don't have anymore time for tech solutions to #climatechange. https://t.co/edlRnGt4Uj

@GlobalEcoGuy @andrewstuhl Sure China and India need to reduce their emissions. But per capita they are still dramatically less than U.S. and Canada.
North America & Western Europe need to take responsibility for #climatechange and take the lead on making dramatic emissions reductions.
Canada has 4th highest per capita greenhouse gas emissions. It's our responsibility to make reductions to the global average at least. #ClimateChange is an issue of inequality first and foremost.

#Saskatchewan @PremierScottMoe believes we need to take meaningful action on #climatechange. He opposes a #CarbonTax, but offers nothing better in Prairie Reslience plan.
It's time to replace his govnt & have a meaningful conversation in this province.

New York City's ambitious plan to fight #climatechange by forcing large buildings to sharply reduce their greenhouse gas emissions.

I'm undecided in the debate over whether individual actions have meaningful impacts on addressing #climatechange. But the argument that flying less has an effect by influencing others & shifting what’s viewed as “normal” is compelling.

How to discuss #climatechange so people will listen. Begin with showing respect for what's important to others and then connecting the dots between what others care about and a changing climate.

To mark his 30th, @_JustinFisher_ reflects on three decades of climate action. In all that very long time, people left tackling #climatechange up to politicians. They failed. Today people are actively participating, guiding what those choices need to be.

Poor @PremierScottMoe. He knows he needs to talk about #ClimateChange, but he's having a tough time getting the basic science right. Less fossil fuels, Mr. Moe, not more..
